endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Agent-specific guardrails (for autonomous solutions): Develop action allow-lists, environment isolation, dryrun modes for high-impact actions, and per-action audit logs.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether allow-lists, environment isolation, dry-run modes, or per-action audit logs prevent irreversible or untraceable harm from autonomous AI agents in health care. The recommendation currently rests on one governance framework (CHAI) that lists these controls as a must.

perspectives.view: The evidence base for this recommendation contains zero studies that test the practice and zero studies that document the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The single endorsement reflects expert consensus within a framework and does not supply effect estimates for any of the four controls.

The only support comes from the CHAI governance playbooks, which classify agent-specific guardrails as a must. This is a voluntary framework and not a statute or FDA requirement. Deployers adopting these controls would be following consensus guidance whose effect on patient harm has not been measured in the studies supplied here.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that deploy autonomous agents in clinical or administrative health care workflows with and without reversibility bounds, and that measure rates of irreversible erroneous actions, time to detect and reverse errors, and completeness of audit trails. No study in this map documents how often agent actions cause irreversible or untraceable harm, so the baseline size of the hazard is also unknown.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested this practice in any population, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy patients. Whether these controls work equally well in under-resourced settings, where staff may have less capacity to review dry-run outputs or audit logs, remains untested.
